question.worked_solution:
If we plug in $x=2$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{({x}^{2}-3)^{2}-8x+15}{{x}^{2}-4x+4} & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{[({x}^{2}-3)^{2}-8x+15]}^{′}}{{[{x}^{2}-4x+4]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{4x({x}^{2}-3)-8}{2x-4}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{({x}^{2}-3)^{2}-8x+15}{{x}^{2}-4x+4} & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{4x({x}^{2}-3)-8}{2x-4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{[4x({x}^{2}-3)-8]}^{′}}{{[2x-4]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{4({x}^{2}-3)+8{x}^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4({2}^{2}-3)+8(2)^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4+32}{2} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
